agi2.what: two-pass pooled selection, kernel version 15 -- the crash-fixed build. Versions 12 and 14 were byte-identical pushes of the same arm and both died 43 minutes in (ValueError: truth value of an array; the pooled merge treated candidate *grids* as sample dicts). Neither wrote submission.json, so neither was ever submittable: yesterday's 'unverifiable' run was a crash, not a pending one.
agi2.decision_dependency: weak. Monotone by construction (attempt_1 is pass A's top-1), so the only observable is attempt_2 and the score cannot lose a task the single-pass build would have scored. A reading inside 29.90 +/- 0.64 with pass B having run falsifies a second decode round as a win; outside the band is the only evidence it buys anything.

predeclared.30.56 < x <= 30.97: replaces the pair's second member; selection becomes 30.97 + x.
predeclared.<= 30.56: record the draw, pair unchanged. With pass B having run this is the predeclared null, not evidence about the method (n=1).

agi2.rehearsal_gate: The commit-mode run was read BEFORE the slot was spent: status COMPLETE 05:16Z, log contains '[two-pass] pooled 5 outputs from both passes' and '[two-pass] attempt_1 pinned to pass A's top-1', no traceback, submission.json written (23,253 bytes). Its 4-task preflight 'Reload score' reads 3.0 against 2.5 for the same preflight on the base build -- five outputs, so not evidence, recorded because it is the number that exists.
agi2.known_defect: Reading the emitted worker (agi2/out/nvarc-p2-fix/arc_solver_emitted.py:338): pass_id and dir_outputs are worker-local and only the worker that draws the __PASS2__ marker flips them, so ONE of four workers decodes a decorrelated pass B while the others re-decode pass B's copies with pass A's seeds. Genuine second-pass coverage is therefore a fraction of the task set, and a null today is a null for the partial design. Fixed the same day and staged as agi2/out/twopass-itemid (pass id travels in the queue item); not pushed, to avoid replacing version 16's log and taking a GPU session.
